rules: 508.1d The active player checks each creature they control to see whether it’s affected by any requirements (effects that say a creature attacks if able, or that it attacks if some condition is met). If the number of requirements that are being obeyed is fewer than the maximum possible number of requirements that could be obeyed without disobeying any restrictions, the declaration of attackers is illegal. If a creature can’t attack unless a player pays a cost, that player is not required to pay that cost, even if attacking with that creature would increase the number of requirements being obeyed. If a requirement that says a creature attacks if able during a certain turn refers to a turn with multiple combat phases, the creature attacks if able during each declare attackers step in that turn.
508.1g If there are any optional costs to attack with the chosen creatures (expressed as costs a player may pay “as” a creature attacks), the active player chooses which, if any, they will pay.

508.1h If any of the chosen creatures require paying costs to attack, or if any optional costs to attack were chosen, the active player determines the total cost to attack. Costs may include paying mana, tapping permanents, sacrificing permanents, discarding cards, and so on. Once the total cost is determined, it becomes “locked in.” If effects would change the total cost after this time, ignore this change.

510.1. First, the active player announces how each attacking creature assigns its combat damage, then the defending player announces how each blocking creature assigns its combat damage. This turn-based action doesn’t use the stack. A player assigns a creature’s combat damage according to the following rules:
723.3. Only control of the player changes. All objects are controlled by their normal controllers. A player who’s being controlled during their turn is still the active player.

723.5. While controlling another player, a player makes all choices and decisions the controlled player is allowed to make or is told to make by the rules or by any objects. This includes choices and decisions about what to play, and choices and decisions called for by spells and abilities.
723.5a The controller of another player can use only that player’s resources (cards, mana, and so on) to pay costs for that player.
723.9. An effect may give a player control of themselves. That player will make their own decisions and choices as normal.

At most 128 legal candidate declarations and the existing shared deadline bound search. Whole-group and individual variants do not enumerate every legal mixed-defender attack or banding/optional combat choice.

Fixed-beneficiary scoring survives control expiry and loss; actor ownership, teams and resources are unchanged. Primary heuristic ControlPlayer dispatch is still unsupported for the three source-bound probes. Full-mode admission remains a separate maintained positive control.

The current actor's ordinary declaration is refined. Different declaring players, controlled blocking, arbitrary mandatory choices, cyclic/custom controllers and human-agent conversion remain unverified.

Candidate rollouts use native payment, triggers, blocking and damage through the second main phase. Incomplete nonterminal rollouts are excluded. Random provider restoration and timeout recovery are checked; stochastic future effects and all hidden information contexts remain unverified.

Worst Fears uses eight mana; Secret uses its normal four-blue cost without optional waterbend payment. Chain/self contexts additionally use native controller APIs, not complete card-generated control-chain proofs.
Unmapped callback diagnostics still need ordinary CLI report aggregation. Hidden/merged/perpetual state, suspended continuations and complete Commander interactions require more work.

Catalog construction confirms script availability rather than full gameplay correctness. Seven unavailable entries are nonstarting meld results. Retained versioned rules are not a current-rules audit.
